meaning: A labelled source row carrying no numeric value at all: a heading, a note or a footnote line inside the parser's region. Written by the ICC/EVE and FX-operations parsers since schema 12. Nothing is lost, because there was nothing on the row to read.

A row whose period label the parser does not recognise and which does carry numbers. This is real data the parser cannot place in time, so the FX parser escalates it to a hard stop rather than discarding it; the reason is declared here because the row is written before the stop and a reader will find it.
The row's date column is blank or does not parse under the source's declared format. The row names no period and cannot be placed in time.
A numeric column holds a value that is present but is not a number: partial tokens such as 12abc, malformed decimals such as 1.2.3, or a unit written into the cell. Never silently reinterpreted.

A column the grain depends on is blank -- the currency or instrument of a trade, or the maturity, currency or rating of a curve node. The row is a real publisher record that cannot be placed on the grain at all. Note that a blank *measure* is not this: since schema 37 a securities trade with no reported volume is accepted with a null volume and volume_status = not_reported, because a trade with an unknown size is still a trade.
The row names a currency outside the set the source contract declares.
A value is outside the range the source contract declares as possible. Both CSV parsers escalate their range guards to a hard stop instead of rejecting the row, so nothing carries this reason today.
The row repeats a key the grain requires to be unique and no ordinal rule resolves it. Securities trades resolve repeats with a duplicate ordinal, so nothing carries this reason today.
